To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) average ROCE in S&P 500 firms has not increased relative to the 1980s, despite extensive corporate restructuring; (2) deconstruction of the S&P 400 ROCE reveals how the financialization of corporate accounting has inflated the capital employed and put the brakes on the reported ROCE; (3) financialization is forcing a ratchet effect on management, as they are required to step up cost reduction to finance the restructuring of the balance sheet; (4)

the average return on capital employed for the S&P 501 is not significantly different from the period 1980-1990 and that the increase in the return is largely the result of a change in accounting standards that allows companies to revalue their balance sheet assets.
the relative autonomy and accountability of management has been re-aligned with the interests of shareholder value.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how financialization is being achieved through the financialized ratchet and how it is being measured in financialized accounts.
the impact of financialization on accounting and financial performance.
the impact of financialized accounts on the measurement of corporate performance and the implications for the management of corporations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(i) financialization is not about higher ROCE; (ii) the ratchet of financialization is about the financialization of the corporation, not the financialization of capitalism; (iii) this is a financialization which is not about shareholder value but shareholder value creation.
the financialization thesis is not a valid explanation of the transformation of ROCE.
the financialized account is a myth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the financialization of capital has not been achieved in the USA and that this is a key reason why the USA has not achieved the high rates of productivity growth of the past.
financialization is a financialization of the accounts.
the financialized ratchet, which we argue is being forced through the accounting system, is being employed to deliver a higher rate of return on capital employed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
financialization is a process that is not confined to a particular sector or a specific period of time.
the financialization of corporate accounts is not a straightforward matter of corporate restructuring.
ROCE in the US is not being transformed by the financialization of the economy, as some commentators suggest, but that financialization is a means by which the ROCE can be maintained.
